sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, polyuria, altered consciousness. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_diagnoses: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with ketoacidosis without coma (E11.10). Secondary diagnoses: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit (J69.0), Acute embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep veins of unspecified lower extremity (I82.409).
sections.discharge_instructions: Drink plenty of fluids. Get adequate rest and avoid overexertion. Follow up with PCP in 7-10 days. Complete prescribed medications as directed. Check blood glucose 4-6 times daily; check urine or blood ketones if BG >250 mg/dL. Return to ER for BG >300 mg/dL with ketones, persistent vomiting, deep breathing, or altered mental status. Follow diabetic diet plan; maintain hydration especially during illness (small sips frequently). Gradual return to normal activity.
sections.follow_up: Follow up with PCP in 7-10 days.
sections.hospital_course: Length of stay: 3 days (primary reason: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, polyuria, altered consciousness). Main treatment: antimicrobials (Ampicillin/Sulbactam); antithrombotic therapy (Enoxaparin); insulin (Insulin, Regular, Human); other parenteral drugs (Potassium Chloride). Key procedures: Central venous catheter insertion (2024-06-15). Complications during stay: aspiration pneumonia (onset hospital day 3), DVT (onset hospital day 3). Significant results: glucose 551 mg/dL [critical] on hospital day 1, treated with Insulin, Regular, Human; pH 7.04 [critical] on hospital day 1; Na 150 mmol/L [H] (prior 146; hypernatremia) on hospital day 3. Medication changes from admission: started Insulin Glargine. Vital signs at discharge: BP 113/72 mmHg, HR 101 bpm, RR 22 /min, SpO2 96% (RA), T 36.7°C. Condition at discharge: discharged home, Barthel Index 80/100.

sections.adl_assessment: Barthel Index 80/100 → minimal assistance (Feeding 10, Bathing 5, Mobility 10, Toilet use 5)
sections.care_plan: Care plan: Nursing problem: deficient fluid volume. Goal: Dehydration and hyperglycemia are corrected and glucose and electrolytes are stable. Observation: Measure I/O hourly and check glucose and serum K every 1-2 hours; Observe mental status and Kussmaul respiration continuously. Care: Coordinate IV rate titration with the physician; Look for an infection source (urine / lower respiratory tract) and record the temperature trend. Education: Explain hypo- and hyperglycemia symptoms and ask the patient to report feeling unwell early. Comorbidity and risk measures: glucose monitoring; hypoglycemia surveillance.
